answer: Each agent locks a unique atlas deposit of spendable stake for two full epochs. Identity then grows as a vine of sequential work receipts rooted in that deposit; peers attest only the vine whose receipt hash matches the published atlas entry. If two vines share a funding bridge—the same payment origin or key lineage—peers slash both deposits and freeze further attestations. A sybil farm must therefore lock fresh capital per fake identity and wait out the lock, or lose the entire stake when a shared bridge is proven on-ledger.
